findings.title: Task 1's unindexed `[~]` fixture line matches neither regex, so Task 5's assertions are unreachable
findings.description:
Task 1 (task file lines 40-41) prescribes `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.`, with no `**bold**` name. Its success text (lines 43-45) reserves the bold-wrap "for the indexed form" only.

- `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` requires `\*\*([^(].*?)\*\*`, so after Task 2's widening the line is still silently dropped.
- The example copies the Future Work item shape (`sample-slice-plan.md:32`), which is `futureWorkParser` format, not a slice-plan entry.
- The slice design defines the unindexed form as `N. [~] **Name** — rationale` (slice line 266).

With the fixture as written the parser yields 6 entries and `completedSlices` 4. Task 5 (lines 91-98) asserts an unindexed deprecated entry, `totalSlices: 7` and `completedSlices: 5`. The implementer is left with a red test and no instruction, and the unindexed success criterion (slice lines 266-268) goes unproven.

Fix: specify the line as `7. [~] **Feature Epsilon** — cut for scope.`

findings.title: Extending `sample-slice-plan.md` breaks existing tests the plan never updates, and Task 5's commit lands on a red suite
findings.description:
Task 5 only names the `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` test for update. Adding entries to this shared fixture breaks more than that.

With only the indexed line parsing (fixture as written):
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:10` — `toHaveLength(5)` fails.
- `ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` — `expect(result.totalSlices).toBe(5)` fails. No task mentions this file.

Once the unindexed line is corrected to parse, it gets `index: 1` from `unindexedCounter` and sorts to `entries[0]` (`slicePlanParser.ts:91`). That additionally breaks:
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:12-20` — `entries[0]` is no longer 101.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:22-30` — `entries[2]` is now 102, not 103.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:126-129` — "tags every entry indexSource: explicit when the plan uses only the indexed format" fails, because the fixture is now mixed.
- `slicePlanParser.test.ts:164-168` — `entries[0]`/`entries[1]` descriptions shift.

Task 5's success command is filtered to `slicePlanParser`, so the commit at line 105 lands with `ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts` red. That is only discovered at Task 13.

The approach also contradicts the slice's last success criterion (slice lines 280-282): regression-freedom is "proven by the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged."

Fix: use the sibling-fixture option the slice already allows (slice lines 220-222), e.g. `deprecated-slice-plan.md`. Leave `sample-slice-plan.md` and its tests untouched. This also removes the need for Task 5's second and third bullets.

findings.title: Task 8's claim about `resolveEntryStatus`'s caller is wrong; widening one `Pick` breaks the build
findings.description:
Task 8 (lines 146-149) says the only caller "passes a full `SlicePlanEntry`". The only caller is `resolveEntryStatusSafe` (line 740), which forwards its own parameter typed `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>` (line 736). Widening only line 694 makes line 740 a type error, because `status` is missing.

Fix: state that both `Pick`s (lines 694 and 736) must gain `'status'`.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is dead code, and the failure path it describes is unhandled
findings.description:
Task 9 (lines 155-163) says the initializer is "the fallback used if `detectDocuments` throws" and that without the change a filesystem error "would incorrectly report it as `not-started`". Neither is true:

- The `catch` at lines 125-127 unconditionally assigns `'degraded'`.
- The success path assigns at lines 122-124.
- The initializer value is therefore never observed.

Cut the bullet; it adds a scattered comparison for no behaviour.

The real failure path is different. A `[~]` entry whose leftover design doc has an unrecognized status, or whose task file is unreadable, resolves to `'degraded'` (`slice.ts:122-123`). `isNext` does not exclude `degraded` (`slice.ts:130-135`, `143-148`), so the entry is marked `← next`. The navigator has the same shape: `WorkflowNavigator.ts:710-714` throws before `deriveEntryStatus` runs.

That conflicts with "never marks it `← next`" (slice lines 272-273) and with Decision 4's "definitionally true regardless of what a stale task file or slice-design frontmatter says". If the failure path matters, short-circuit on `entry.status === STATUS.Deprecated` before the I/O at both sites and add a test. Otherwise drop the bullet and record the limitation.

findings.title: A second `completedSlices` computation is not updated
findings.description:
Task 4 changes only the parser, relying on the slice's claim that `completedSlices` "is computed once, in the parser" (slice lines 234-235). The `introspection_slice_plan` tool recomputes it after worktree range filtering as `entries.filter((e) => e.isChecked).length`.

With a `worktreeId`, a plan that is all `[x]`/`[~]` reports `completedSlices < totalSlices`. Without one, it reports them equal. That leaves the third success criterion (slice lines 269-271) unmet on this surface.

Fix: add a step to Task 4 that applies the same predicate here, ideally via one exported helper rather than a third copy.

findings.title: Task 12 cannot fail, and nothing tests `completedSlices === totalSlices` through the real parser
findings.description:
Task 12 sends the implementer to the existing `plan-status-vs-entries` tests (lines 795-849). Those inject a hand-written `SlicePlanResult` through `makeMockIntrospector`. The file also replaces `node:fs/promises` with a `readdir`-only mock (lines 31-33), so the real `parseSlicePlan` cannot be used there.

The new case will hard-code `totalSlices: 2, completedSlices: 2`. It passes identically with Task 4 reverted, so it does not prove Decision 3 reaches the rule.

The underlying equality is also untested:
- Task 4's own success line (task lines 82-83) and slice lines 269-271 require "all checked or deprecated → `completedSlices === totalSlices`".
- Task 5's fixture retains unchecked 103/104, so it never asserts equality.
- The `arch-status-vs-plans` half of slice lines 277-279 is not mentioned.

Fix:
- Add an all-resolved real-format plan (every line `[x]` or `[~]`) to Task 5 and assert equality on the parser output.
- Either drop Task 12 (the existing rule tests plus that parser assertion cover the criterion) or rebuild it in a separate file. That file would use the real `ArtifactIntrospector` on a scratch directory and cover both rules.

findings.title: `[~]` entries now enter per-entry ConsistencyChecker rules that treat them as plain unchecked
findings.description:
Today a `[~]` line is absent from `entries`, so `checkAll` never visits it (lines 102-124). After Tasks 2-3 it is visited with `isChecked: false`. No task guards or tests the consequences:

- **`ruleTaskVsPlan` lines 338-347:** a slice descoped mid-implementation (task file partly checked) gets a permanent, non-fixable "Tasks in progress but slice N is unchecked in plan" warning. Only hand-editing the task file ends it.
- **`ruleTaskVsPlan` lines 302-316:** a `[~]` entry with a complete task file gets a fixable `update-checkbox` (`checked: true`) finding. `updateCheckbox` throws on a `[~]` line (`markdownWriter.ts:21-26`), so every `cf check --fix` records a `fixErrors` entry (line 234) and the finding never clears.
- **`rulePlanVsFrontmatter` lines 498-511 and `ruleInitiativeEntryVsArch` lines 905-918:** same shape. Initiative plans go through the same parser (line 164).
- **`ruleReviewGate` lines 650-651:** `preTasks`/`preImplementation` gates now evaluate for a deprecated entry that has docs.

The slice puts ConsistencyChecker rule changes out of scope (slice lines 233-236), but these are new false positives on exactly the entries this slice makes visible. Add a task that skips per-entry rules when `planEntry.status === STATUS.Deprecated`, with one test. Otherwise list the behaviour explicitly as accepted, with a follow-up.

findings.title: Other plan-entry consumers are left on checkbox-only derivation, so `[~]` reads differently by surface
findings.description:
The plan threads `planLineStatus` into two `deriveEntryStatus` call sites. Others also feed it parsed plan entries:

- **`arch.ts:99`, `112`, `114` (`cf list arch`):** a `[~]` initiative-plan line used to be invisible. It will now be listed as `○ not started`.
- **`ProjectModelBuilder.ts:445`:** a planned-but-unwritten `[~]` slice becomes `not-started` in the model.
- **`ProjectModelBuilder.ts:487`:** this one copies `entry.status` directly, so plan-only initiatives become `deprecated`.

The same marker therefore yields three different answers. Either add the one-line `planLineStatus` argument at these sites in Tasks 8/9, or record them as known follow-ups so Task 13's "no regressions" check is not read as covering them.

findings.title: Task 11 leaves the scenario open and names an outcome the mirrored setup cannot produce
findings.description:
Task 11 says to mirror the test at `WorkflowNavigator.test.ts:1073` (which uses `fileSlice: ''`) and assert it "skips past to the next genuine candidate (or reports the plan/initiative complete if none remain)".

- With no active slice and no remaining candidate, `getNext` returns "Pick your first slice…" with `cf set slice <index>` (lines 239-249), not a plan-complete message.
- "Slice plan complete" is only produced on the active-slice-complete path (lines 357-384).

An implementer choosing the "none remain" variant gets a failing test. Task 11 (lines 192-194) tells them to treat that as a design error.

Fix: pin both cases.
- `[x] 125 / [~] 127 / [ ] 130` with `fileSlice: ''` → `cf set slice 130`.
- An active complete slice with `[~]` as the only other entry → the "Slice plan complete" recommendation.

The second case is what covers the second half of slice lines 274-276.

findings.title: CLI build and test consume core from `dist`, but Tasks 9-10 never say to rebuild core
findings.description:
`@context-forge/cli` resolves `@context-forge/core` through `dist/` (`main`/`exports`). `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` has no `paths` or `references`, and there is no CLI vitest config aliasing to source.

- Task 9's "builds clean" does not name a command.
- Task 10's command is CLI-only.

With a stale core `dist`, `planLineStatus` is an unknown-property compile error in `slice.ts`. The Task 10 test then sees `[~]` lines still dropped (`parsed.entries[0]` undefined), which looks like the wiring is wrong.

Fix: state `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` (or `pnpm -r build`) as an explicit step before Task 9's build and Task 10's test.

findings.title: Tasks 2-4 are over-split, Task 5 carries a redundant test, and Task 8 is committed before its test
findings.description:
- **Tasks 2, 3, 4:** together they change about six lines in one function. Task 2's "both regexes match a `[~]` line" and Task 3's "no new field added" cannot be checked until Task 5. Merge them into one implementation task followed by Task 5.
- **Task 5, third bullet (lines 99-102):** it re-asserts what `slicePlanParser.test.ts:8-31` and `42-46` already pin. With a sibling fixture those tests are the regression proof, so cut it.
- **Task 8:** its only test is Task 11, but Tasks 9-10 and the commit at line 179 sit in between. Reorder to 8 → 11 → 9 → 10 so each wiring change is tested before it is committed.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description:
Lines 105, 135, 179, 197, 212 and 224 are `- [ ] Commit: …` sub-items. Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checklist items.

Placement is otherwise reasonable (after each implementation+test pair). The exception is line 105, which is not a green point until the fixture finding above is fixed.

findings.title: User-facing strings will describe deprecated entries as "checked" or "complete"
findings.description:
After Task 4, `completedSlices` includes deprecated entries, but several messages still interpolate it with "checked"/"complete" wording:

- `ConsistencyChecker.ts:738`, `754`, `837`, `853`, `990`, `1006` — "only X/Y entries are checked", "All N entries are checked".
- `ArtifactIntrospector.ts:90` — "X of Y slices complete".
- `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:60`.

No success criterion requires a wording change; this is recorded for the implementer.
